data.title: Generated Content Lowers the Cost of Credible Pretexts
data.summary:
The public detail available about the organisation is sufficient to generate fluent,
context-accurate pretext material and plausible supporting personas at negligible cost.
data.description:
The traditional indicators staff were taught to rely on — poor language, generic greetings,
obvious inconsistency — no longer separate a real message from a fabricated one. Generated
content is fluent, correctly uses internal terminology drawn from public sources, and can be
produced at volume.

Supporting personas follow the same economics. A profile with a coherent history, plausible
imagery and consistent activity can be assembled cheaply, which removes the verification
value of a profile simply existing and looking established.

The defensive implication is that awareness training built on spotting defects is obsolete,
and the organisation's resistance has to come from process — verification that does not
depend on judging whether a message feels right.
data.recommendation:
* Rewrite awareness material around verification behaviour rather than around spotting
  language defects, which no longer distinguish anything.
* Require out-of-band verification for consequential requests regardless of how plausible
  the approach appears.
* Make reporting a suspicion socially safe, since the individual judgement that training
  previously relied on is no longer reliable.
data.short_recommendation: Base awareness on verification behaviour, not on spotting language defects.
